error: The analysis code writes the headline as a literal instead of reading the metrics registry; the number happens to be right.
warning_texts: src/analysis/build_claims.py line 53 hard-codes the headline net revenue (35741.52) as a literal instead of reading metrics.net_revenue.value, so the claim register would not follow a corrected or refreshed metrics registry even though its source_value_ref says it does.

The check plan has no rule that compares a claim's value with the value its source_value_ref resolves to (claim_refs_resolve only proves the ref exists), so a hard-coded or stale claim value passes gate_claims_machine whenever it happens to equal the raw recompute; this binding is checked only by au

The population period ends 2025-03-30 while the metrics period is named 2025-Q1-delivered and R01 speaks of the reported quarter; raw_data/orders.csv has no 2025-03-31 rows, so no figure changes, but a reader may take the figures as the full calendar Q1.

CLM-REFUND-RATE's caveat names the basis with the identifier paying_customers (denominator is unique paying_customers, not order rows); it satisfies the frozen customers-not-rows topic and states customers rather than rows, but a release rendering it verbatim shows an identifier rather than plain wo

On the order-row basis the refund rate would be 0.189655 (33 of 174 rows) against the published 0.473684 (27 of 57 paying customers); the claim is correct under the spec ruling, and the size of the gap is why the basis caveat must survive into the release.
summary: All five claims recompute from raw_data/orders.csv to exactly the registered values (35741.52, 0.473684 on 27/57 paying customers, PL 11181.67, DE 11032.61, CZ 13527.24), and the machine gate's recalc is rooted in raw only; but CLM-NET-REVENUE's value is a string literal in src/analysis/build_claims.py:53 rather than the metrics.net_revenue.value its source_value_ref declares, so the claim is not bound to the registry and no rule in the check plan detects it.
